items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:40:1
items.html: The light is Mati in Keter, and then the light of Hochma and Bina both rise there: For Hochma returned and refined from the coarseness of phase two in the screen within her, and then the lights departed from there and rose to Keter, as above. And this caused an awakening of the coarseness in the Nukva of Keter, by the force of the record of the male of Hochma that rose within her, which is phase three; and therefore she returned and received her coarseness of phase three, and once again the level of Hochma expanded to her, and the light of Hochma is Mati in the vessel of Keter. And know that the ARI calls the refinement of the coarseness by the name of a craving to rise to the upper one, for refinement and ascent are one and the same.

items.html:
Two distances, Bina and Hochma, in which there is no light. In order to explain the matter of these two distances, which came about because of the ascent of HB to Keter, and so that it be possible to continue the explanation of the words of the ARI, I must be lengthy here, in order to explain well, with fundamental understanding, the nature of those ten vessels that remained from the first expansion of AK after the departure of their lights from within them, and that came and were fixed here in the Partzuf of the second expansion of AK. And chiefly one must understand well the matter of the face and the posterior of those vessels. For up to here we have explained only from the aspect of the coarseness in the screen that couples with the upper light, where the greatest coarseness in the degree is its face, and the lesser measure of coarseness in it is in the posterior of the degree. And now we shall explain the face and the posterior in the nature of the vessels themselves, that is, according to how they were imprinted by the expansion and the departure of the first expansion. For the chief revelation of the forces in the ways of the lights comes for the most part through the nature of the vessels themselves, and this is why the vessels are called pipes: they resemble the nature of water, which receives its form through the pipes by which it is drawn — whether abundantly or restrictedly, whether eastward or westward, and so forth. And likewise the lights are acted upon by the nature of the vessels in which they are clothed. Therefore we must understand them thoroughly.
And you find that the light of Keter that is in the first expansion did not descend back into the second expansion, but remained standing in the Rosh, beneath the Malchut of the Rosh. And at the time when the ZON of the vessel of Keter of the second expansion must rise to receive their abundance, it turns its face to them, that is, it bestows to them all their need — but only while they are still with it in the Malchut of the Rosh. However, after they have been filled with their abundance and descend to the Guf, it immediately turns its posterior to them, which means that it withholds from them the abundance they need.
And this must be understood: if it turns back and withholds the abundance from them, what did they gain by the ascent to the Rosh? However, the matter is that in truth they received all their need at the time of the ascent, that is, according to the screens in them, which are phase four of the male and phase three of the female, whose level of coupling is close to the level of Keter, and they descended to the Keter of the Guf with all this great abundance. If so, one must understand what that root Keter accomplished by turning its posterior toward the ZON of Keter that descended to the Guf. Yet it accomplishes a great deal thereby, for because of it the vessel of Keter of the Guf, too, must be found in the aspect of the posterior toward Hochma. Since this vessel is in truth the vessel of that same root Keter from the time of the first expansion — for it was from her that it departed and rose to the Rosh — it therefore acts upon her even while it is in the Rosh, so that she becomes equal to it as it stands in the Rosh. And therefore the vessel, too, must be in the aspect of the posterior toward all the nine Sefirot below her. That is, she does not give them of that abundance she received in the Rosh except by way of the posterior, which means with the withholding of the illumination of Hochma from them, for Hochma is always called the light of the face, or the light of GAR. And remember this for all places. So that the nine lower Sefirot cannot receive from Keter anything but the aspect of VAK, which means with a lack of the illumination of Hochma. And understand this well.
And the meaning of the face and the posterior of the vessels is simple: the place of bestowal in it is called face, and that aspect which does not bestow through it is called posterior. This resembles a person who deals with his fellow: he stands opposite him at his front side, and not behind him. And with this you will understand that although Keter bestows by way of its posterior, it is possible at times to call it by the name of face, even though there is no illumination of Hochma in it — namely, in respect of its being a place of bestowal. Therefore the matter is to be understood only according to the subject under discussion.
Therefore, when the screen of Keter refines from the coarseness of phase four and phase three within it to phase three and phase two, which is fit for the light of Hochma, as above, the vessel of Keter must turn her face downward and her posterior upward, since her posterior detains the illumination of Hochma altogether, by reason of the root Keter of the Rosh that stands beneath the Malchut of the Rosh, as above. However, what causes this turning of the face is the matter of the refinement of the screen of the male of Keter, which is the secret of the record that the root Keter left in this vessel of Keter after its departure from her. And since this record departed from there — for it refined and came to the coarseness of phase three — the rule of the root Keter over its own vessel ceased, and then the vessel turns her face downward. And then everything that belongs to the illumination of the root Keter returns and rises to it, to the Rosh; and its remainder, that is, the record of phase three of the first expansion, which is the secret of the male of Hochma, together with the illumination of the new coupling that emerged on the coarseness of phase three that the Nukva of Keter left after her refinement, becomes the female of the vessel of Hochma, as above.
And now we shall explain the face and the posterior of the vessel of Hochma. For it is the way of Hochma to bestow only Hochma, and therefore the place of the bestowal of Hochma is her face, and the place of the bestowal of the light of Hassadim is her aspect of the posterior — that is, exactly the opposite of Keter, from one extreme to the other. For the face of Keter is to bestow VAK, and the illumination of GAR is in her posterior, as above; whereas the face of Hochma is the illumination of GAR from the aspect of the light of Hochma, and her posterior is the illumination of VAK, as explained.
And the face and the posterior of the vessel of Bina are likewise the opposite of the vessel of Hochma, though not a complete opposite, since Bina is at her root the very essence of Hochma, except that it is her nature always to crave the light of Hassadim, as the ARI writes before us in the secret of the words “for He delights in Hesed,” for Bina is called “Hu” [He] and desires and craves Hassadim. (And the reason for this was already explained in Part 1, in the Inner Light, study it there.) Therefore, when she has Hassadim in the Partzuf, she returns and becomes the very essence of Hochma, as the ARI wrote above in the secret of Aba and Ima dwelling as one and emerging as one, study it there. However, the vessel of Bina is discerned chiefly from the side of her craving for Hassadim, and therefore her face is the illumination of Hassadim and her posterior is the illumination of Hochma — that is, the opposite of the vessel of Hochma.
And now we shall explain in brief the vessels of the seven lower Sefirot, HGT NHYM. And you must remember the words of the ARI above (Part 4, Chapter 6, item 8), that there is in ZA no more than “only five ends, which are five Hassadim, from Hesed to Hod; but Yesod does not take a particular Hesed for itself, only that all five ends are included in it.” And for the explanation of these words, study it there in the Inner Light. And the essence of it is that there are two general lights in all the degrees, which are the light of Hochma and the light of Hassadim; and there are also five phases of coarseness in the screen, according to the five phases of direct light, which are called KHB, Tifferet and Malchut. And these five phases are called KHB TM only when the GAR are the aspect of the light of Hochma; but where these five phases have in them nothing but the light of Hassadim alone, they are called HGT NH, for the first three phases, KHB, have their names changed to HGT, and the last two phases, Tifferet and Malchut, have their names changed to Netzah and Hod. And this is what he says, “which are five Hassadim, from Hesed to Hod,” that is, that even the first three phases are likewise only the light of Hassadim, and not at all the light of Hochma. Understand and remember this. And Yesod and Malchut are merely two inclusive ones of the above five ends: one inclusive one from the side of their being five Hassadim sweetened in the quality of mercy, and one inclusive one from the side of their being in the quality of judgment, when they are called five Gvurot, or when the five Hassadim and the five Gvurot are included together, as is written before us.
However, in order to understand the nature of these five ends, we need the words of the ARI here concerning Mati and Lo Mati, for they are not explained in any other place in all the writings of the ARI. Therefore these words of his require great attention.
And let us return to explaining the birth of the first Hesed of these five Hassadim, brought in the words of the ARI on page 321, item 37: that after the ZON of Hochma departed to Keter — for the coarseness of phase two refined to phase one, whose coupling raises nothing but the light of VAK, which are now included in the first Hesed — then the vessel of Hochma turned its face downward, for it annulled its aspect of the face and turned its posterior upward. That is, its former posterior, which means the illumination of Hassadim, as above, now became the place of bestowal, and thereby it equalized itself with the face of Bina, as above in the secret of the words “for He delights in Hesed.” And then it gave her the seven lights that are now included in the light of the first Hesed. And the light of Hesed is found in the vessel of Bina.
And you must remember that besides this light of Hesed there are two further lights that precede it in that vessel of Bina. They are: the male born of the coupling of the ZON of the vessel of Hochma, which is in truth phase two, which is the level of the light of Bina, like the female of Hochma herself; but since it was born through the turning of the face of the vessel of Hochma, as above in the words of the ARI, item 35, and in the Inner Light there, the passage beginning “Hochma turned,” it is therefore discerned as the aspect of the VAK of Hochma. And know that it is the root of Israel Saba in all the Partzufim. And there is there a second light, which is the record of the vessel of Bina that has been there since the time of the first expansion. (For besides the screen being included from all the records that are in those vessels as it passed on to the Emanator, it is certain that the chief records remained in their place, in their own vessels, and did not rise with the screen to the Emanator.) And that record is the aspect of the female that is in the vessel of Bina, and know that she is the root of all the aspects of Tevuna in all the Partzufim. However, this light of Hesed, which Hochma has now bestowed to Bina, is considered the aspect of the son of Bina, and not the aspect of her own self.
And remember well the relation of the ZON that are in the vessel of Hochma to the ZON that are in the vessel of Bina; for in truth they are the light of a single level of Bina, except that the relation of the ZON of Bina to the ZON of Hochma is like the relation of Israel Saba and Tevuna to the upper Aba and Ima, for YESHSUT are only the VAK of Aba and Ima themselves — yet both of them are the aspect of a single level, of the coarseness of phase two. And from here you will understand that the chief purpose of the division of Aba and Ima and YESHSUT into two Partzufim, GAR and VAK, as above, is only to give birth to the Katnut of the seven lower Sefirot. For it is impossible for the vessel of Hochma to bestow the light of Hesed, which is the aspect of VAK lacking GAR, except by way of the posterior of Hochma, and therefore it turns the face into posterior, as above. And this turning is found to divide the vessel of Hochma into two Partzufim: into a Partzuf of GAR, whose face remained in its place, and into a Partzuf of VAK of Hochma, which turned the face into posterior and bestows the light of VAK lacking GAR. And likewise YESHSUT is called VAK, after the turning of the face of the vessel of Hochma, as above.
However, in order to give birth to the Gadlut of ZA, that is, the GAR belonging to those five Hassadim, the vessel of Hochma must return and turn its face upward as at first. And then it is discerned that the ZON of Bina and the ZON of Hochma, which had been divided into GAR and VAK by reason of the turning of the face of Hochma — now that Hochma has returned and annulled this turning of the face, and there is no longer here a bestowal of GAR and a bestowal of VAK in the vessel of Hochma — the ZON of Bina return and rise to the ZON of Hochma, and once more they become a single Partzuf. And know that this applies also in the Partzufim of Atzilut: at the time when Aba and Ima wish to bestow Mochin of GAR to ZA, then Aba and Ima and YESHSUT return and become a single Partzuf. And this too is for the above reason, for the illumination of VAK from Hochma is then annulled and the face returns to its place as at first.
And with all that has been explained you will well understand the order of the birth of the first light of Hesed in its aspect of Gadlut, brought in the words of the ARI on page 323, item 39. And the gist of his words is that it returned to be Lo Mati in Keter, and then Mati in Hochma, that the light of Hochma that had been in Keter descended to Hochma; and then the seven sons that are in Bina are grown; and then Bina rises to Hochma because of the craving she has to cleave to her, and seven lights descend and are given to Hesed face to face. End of quote.
The explanation: for the ZON of Keter refined once more and departed upward to the root Keter that stands beneath the Malchut of the Rosh; and then the vessel of Keter turned its face downward and gave its remainder, which are the ZON of Hochma, to the vessel of Hochma; and the aspect of the face of the ZON of Hochma returned to its place as at first. And then “Bina rises to Hochma,” that is, that Bina and Hochma became a single vessel, in the manner of the upper Aba and Ima with YESHSUT that became a single Partzuf, as above, study it there well. And out of this, that Hesed which is in the vessel of Bina is found to receive the illumination of the light of Hochma, since the vessel is united with the light of Hochma, as above. And Hesed is found to have returned to the aspect of GAR, which is called becoming grown. And this is what he says, “and then the seven sons that are in Bina are grown and do not need their mother,” that is, that they attained the aspect of the illumination of Hochma and of GAR, whereby the seven lower ones are discerned as grown, as explained. And it was already explained above that before the light of Hesed attains Gadlut it cannot expand downward, since it cannot separate from the vessel of Bina, which is all its vitality and its essence from the aspect of GAR, and it is therefore discerned as needing its mother. But now that it has already attained the light of Hochma itself, it no longer needs the nursing of the vessel of Bina. And this is what he says, “and do not need their mother.”
“And then the vessel of Bina turned her face downward, and the seven lights in her descend and are all given to Hesed face to face”: And you must remember that the aspect of the face of the vessel of Bina is for the illumination of Hassadim, and her posterior is for the illumination of Hochma; and while she is in this state she cannot bestow the illumination of the light of Hesed together with the illumination of Hochma, as above. However, it was explained that the restoring of the face of the vessel of Hochma caused the union of the two vessels, Bina with Hochma, into one, since the vessel of Hochma had already annulled her illumination of VAK, as above, study it there. And therefore the vessel of Bina is found to have turned her face, by the force of this union, into posterior, and the posterior that had been before now became the aspect of face. That is, that same posterior which withheld the bestowal of the illumination of Hochma now became a bestower of the illumination of Hochma, since her vessel received that same nature of face and posterior that is in Hochma. And therefore Bina now bestowed the seven lower ones, with the illumination of Hochma, to the vessel of Hesed, face to face.
Now you will thoroughly understand the nature of the Sefira of Hesed of ZA. The aspect of the substance of the vessel of Hesed is the aspect of Keter of the VAK, for it was already explained that the HGT of ZA are a change of name of KHB — only that KHB of the light of Hassadim, that is, the KHB of the level of phase one, are called HGT, as above, study it there. Thus the vessel of Hesed is the aspect of the vessel of Keter of ZA; yet even so it is not considered Keter, but only the aspect of Hochma of ZA. And this is by reason of the light in it, for there is in it no light of Keter at all, but only the illumination of Hochma that it received while it was in the vessel of Bina, at the time when she was united with the vessel of Hochma into a single vessel, as above; and therefore it is called by the name of Hochma. And there are further reasons, and this is not the place to elaborate.
Now we shall explain the order of the emanation of the vessel of Gvura, brought in the words of the ARI here in item 40, and these are his words: “And afterwards the light returns to be Mati in Keter, and then Hochma and Bina both rise there. And then it turns out that there is a great distance between the sons and the light of GAR, for there are between them two distances, Bina and Hochma, in which there is no light. Therefore the light of Hesed then rises to Bina, and this is called Lo Mati in Hesed; and then the vessel of Hesed turns its face and gives the six lights downward, in Gvura.” End of quote.
And you must remember the two matters involved in the turning of the face downward, which were explained above. The first is from the side of the vessel, that is, its place of bestowal — whether the aspect of Hochma, or the aspect of Hassadim and not Hochma. And the second matter is from the side of the aspect of the coupling, in the measure of the coarseness of the screen: the coarsest phase in the degree is discerned as the face, and the phase of coarseness lesser than it is the aspect of the posterior in that same degree. Accordingly it always turns out that the posterior of the upper degree is the face of the lower degree; and therefore it always turns out that when the upper one wishes to bestow to the lower one, it must turn its face downward, which means that it refines from the measure of coarseness in it that is its face, and remains in the aspect of its lesser coarseness, in a measure equal to the coarseness of the lower degree, for then it is discerned as close to it and can bestow in it, as above. And with this you will understand that wherever the matter of the bestowal of Bina to the vessel of Hesed is brought here, Bina has then refined from phase two to phase one, for then she is found face to face with the vessel of Hesed, from the side of the screen in her.
And so, at the time when Bina bestowed the light of Hesed to the vessel of Hesed, Bina had refined to phase one. And there was here a complete order of refinement according to the degrees. For first Keter refined from phase three to phase two, and then the light of Keter vanished to the root, and it gave phase two to the vessel of Hochma, and then the vessel of Bina unites with it as one. And afterwards phase two, too, refined to phase one, and then the lights of the vessels of Hochma and Bina vanished to Keter, and phase one is bestowed to the vessel of Hesed with the illumination of Hochma, as above.
And it was already explained above that when the four lights — the male and female of Hochma and the male and female of Bina — rise to Keter, they awaken in the vessel of Keter the aspect of the coarseness of phase three anew, and once again the ten Sefirot emerge there, by the force of the upper coupling, at the level of Hochma as at first, and the light of Hochma returns to the vessel of Keter. And this is what is called Mati in Keter.
And you find that the arrival of Hesed in its own vessel causes it to be Mati in Keter; for then phase two in HB refines to phase one, and their four lights rise to the vessel of Keter and cause a coupling anew there, on the level of phase three, and again the light of Hochma is Mati in the vessel of Keter as at first. And this is what he says, “the light returns to be Mati in Keter, and then Hochma and Bina both rise there,” that is, as explained, that because of the ascent of the four lights of HB the light is found to be Mati in the vessel of Keter. “And then it turns out that there is a great distance between the sons and the light of GAR, for there are between them two distances.” The explanation: for it was explained that the face of Keter is for the illumination of VAK without GAR, as above, page 324, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “and this must be understood,” study it there well, for the matter is not to be repeated. You also know that the face of the vessel of Bina is likewise for the illumination of VAK without GAR, as above in the secret of “for He delights in Hesed,” as above in the Inner Light, page 325, the passage beginning “and the face,” study it there well. And these are the two distances that now lie upon the light of Hesed and withhold from it the illumination of GAR that it earlier received from Hochma. And this is what he says, “and then it turns out that there is a great distance between the sons and the light of GAR,” that is, that these two posteriors, of Bina and of Keter, greatly distance the GAR from the sons, who are the seven lower ones included in the light of Hesed. And this is what he says, “for there are between them two distances, Bina and Hochma, in which there is no light,” that is, that had there been light in Hochma, it would have been possible for the light of Hesed to receive from Hochma, and the posterior of Bina would not have withheld it from him, since it did not withhold it from him at first. But now, when even in Hochma there is no light, because of the posterior of Keter, that illumination which Hesed earlier received from Hochma is therefore withheld as well.
And this is what he says, “therefore the light of Hesed then rises to Bina.” For after the GAR vanished from the light of Hesed and it returned to its Katnut, it once more needs its mother, Bina, in order to nurse from there the illumination of GAR of the vessel, at least as at first. And this is what he says, “and then the vessel of Hesed turns its face and gives the six lights downward, in Gvura.” For the face of the vessel of Hesed is for the illumination of Hochma, after it received the illumination of Hochma, as above, and its posterior is for the illumination of Hassadim; for in every place where there are Hochma and Hassadim in a degree, Hochma is discerned as the face and Hassadim as the posterior, and therefore the posterior of Hesed is discerned as the illumination of Hassadim. But now that the illumination of Hochma has vanished from it, and its light has vanished into the vessel of Bina, it turns out that it turned its face downward and gave the remainder of the light in it to the vessel of Gvura, and then it is Mati in Gvura.
Now you will thoroughly understand the nature of the Sefira of Gvura of ZA. For the substance of the vessel of Gvura is the aspect of Hochma of the VAK, as was explained above, that the HGT are the aspect of KHB of the VAK; thus the vessel of Gvura is Hochma. Yet it is discerned as the aspect of Bina, and this is because its light is the aspect of the VAK of the illumination of Hochma that is in Hesed, like the ZON of the upper Bina, which are the aspect of the six ends of the upper Hochma. Thus the light of Gvura is the aspect of Bina of the VAK. And so the two Sefirot of ZA have been explained, Hesed and Gvura, which are the aspect of Hochma and Bina of ZA, even though their vessels have the value of Keter and Hochma.
